ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Which stage of a whitefly life cycle follows the third instar nymph?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a circular schematic diagram of the life cycle of a whitefly, with multiple stages connected in sequence by arrows. On the left side there is an adult form, above there is a group of egg-shaped structures, and on the right side and below there are several oval-shaped or spine-protruding nymph forms; the arrows show that these stages cycle in order. Reasoning: The question asks “which stage is after the third instar nymph”. In the life cycle of a whitefly, the nymph instars advance in numerical order: after the first instar, second instar, and third instar is the fourth instar. Therefore, what follows the third instar nymph is the fourth instar nymph.
